findings.title: SEP-45 validate issues a JWT for the contract account in args without checking the client's auth entry
API key compared with non-constant-time String.equals
SEP-45 validate does not bind each auth entry to the web_auth_verify root invocation
Failed Horizon transactions are parsed as successful payments with the declared amount
SEP-45 challenge signs every server-credentialed auth entry returned by the RPC without checking its invocation
Any contract's transfer(from,to,amount) is emitted as an asset transfer without checking the contract is the anchor's asset
Malformed transfer invocation args throw an unchecked exception that aborts conversion of the whole transaction
SEP-10 validation never verifies the client_domain signature for existing accounts
SEP-31 accepts a SEP-38 quote owned by another client account
SEP-10 validation for a nonexistent account accepts any extra signature as the client_domain proof
Client-name attribution is checked only when an Authorization header is supplied
SEP-12 id-path PUT sends a request memo upstream without binding it to the token's memo
SEP-31 customer-id claim runs after the upstream customer write, so a rejected claim still leaves the write applied
SEP-6 exchange accepts a SEP-38 quote created by another account
SEP-24 deposit to a contract account skips the memo_type 'id' rule when memo_type is omitted
Transaction id is concatenated into the REST path without encoding, so a crafted id changes the request path
Domain match overrides the account's own client, so the allowlist can be satisfied by a domain the account does not belong to
Client attribution is resolved from an unproven client_domain string (duplicate root cause of security-ai-control-bypass-1/20/21)
SEP-12 delete skips memo binding for muxed-account tokens, letting a user delete another subaccount's customer
RPC auth header secret is re-sent to any host an RPC endpoint redirects to
Platform and callback credentials are re-sent to any host a configured endpoint redirects to
SEP-31 create saves the transaction before binding the quote, so a race leaves an orphan transaction with a used quote
MEMO_ID accepts negative and out-of-range uint64 values, so the stored memo may differ from the on-chain memo
SEP-45 challenge tells the client which network to sign for using the RPC-reported passphrase, not the configured one
getChallenge indexes simulation results without null or empty checks
hasTrustline treats a deauthorized trustline as present
Empty client_domain with an Authorization header reaches JWT verification with a null key and throws an unhandled error
Horizon hasTrustline counts a deauthorized trustline as present
Horizon hasTrustline lets SDK network errors escape the LedgerException contract
total_price divides by a rate buy amount that may be zero, with no check
getPrice and getPrices dereference the rate response without a null check
SEP-24 deposit and withdraw skip the sign and scale checks that SEP-6 and SEP-31 apply to amounts
RpcHelper crashes with an unchecked exception on empty, non-array or empty-array JSON-RPC bodies
SEP-24 deposit stores the raw request asset_issuer, so omitted issuers are saved as null
SEP-24 transaction-created event is published before the @Transactional method commits
SEP-24 findTransactions throws NullPointerException when asset_code is absent
WebAuthJwtFilter finally block dereferences a null token when both decodes fail
health() builds the checks query and then discards it, so the requested checks are never sent
RPC and PATCH calls drop the endpoint path prefix, unlike the REST GET calls
SEP-6 amount validator skips magnitude bound and leaks raw NumberFormatException
Static amount validator used by SEP-31 has no significant-decimals check
ReflectionUtil.getField does not check that the target is an SSEStream before reading its field
Malformed base64 memo_hash throws an unchecked IllegalArgumentException instead of a validation error
Outbound platform and callback calls have no response-size cap and a 10-minute timeout
SEP-31 strict-send accepts a fee that exceeds the amount and stores a negative amount_out
Soroban RPC submit returns the admission status without polling to a final result
RPC response body is read into memory with no size cap
Platform notifications ignore HTTP and JSON-RPC failures, so a rejected on-chain funds notice reads as success
ReflectionUtil.getField returns the default on any lookup failure, hiding a renamed or inaccessible SDK field
Horizon and Soroban RPC submit paths return the send status without polling to a final state
Legacy G-account rows are readable by every muxed sub-account of that G (findTransaction)
SEP-24 findTransaction legacy branch lets muxed sub-accounts read each other's rows of the same G account
Secret getters are not annotated @Secret, so Log redaction would not cover the SEP-10 signing seed
Client-domain SSRF guard checks DNS once and then fetches the URL with redirects followed
Client-signed SEP-10 header JWT is replayable until exp (no jti, nonce or audience binding)
Asset resolution falls back to code-only match when issuer is omitted
SEP-6 deposit and withdraw enablement is checked by asset code only, not by issuer
SEP-45 signs contract auth entries with the SEP-10 signing seed, so one key serves both protocols

failing_checks.title: Stated purpose versus behaviour
failing_checks.reason: The SEP-24 flow is documented as validating amounts the same way as SEP-6 and SEP-31, but this path applies only min/max limits and skips the sign and scale checks used elsewhere. This is already recorded as reliability-ai-functional-defect-3.

failing_checks.title: Core function works
failing_checks.reason: The SEP-45 challenge uses the RPC-reported passphrase instead of the configured one, so the core function signs for the wrong network if the RPC differs. Already recorded as reliability-ai-functional-defect-10.
